gaps: Per-vessel CLS (cut-off time) is not in the routePort SSR payload. Briefing required CLS; for v0.1 the next-cls command returns ETD instead. Dedicated cut-off field requires a different page (shipDateDetail) we haven't wrapped yet.
New lanes not in the seeded 7 require user capture in browser. Adding a routes import command (scan Chrome history) is v0.2.

narrative.headline: A single-binary CLI for ocean-freight schedules — pulls Weiyun's public port/carrier/fleet APIs and scrapes per-lane sailings from registered routePort URLs.
narrative.value_prop: Carrier discovery (which carriers serve a port, what services they run) goes through Weiyun's clean public APIs; per-week sailings (vessel name, voyage, ETD, capacity, flag) come from /routePort URLs the user captures once in their browser. Both layers are pure HTTP, no encryption reverse-engineering, no resident browser.

quickstart.comment: List all ~200 ports Weiyun knows about.
View registered lanes (auto-seeds 7 representative routes on first run).
Fetch latest schedule for that lane.
Soonest future sailing on that lane.
All carriers' sailings on that lane in ETD order.

troubleshoots.fix: Capture the routePort URL once in your browser, then run: schedule-pp-cli routes add X '<paste URL>' --pol POL --pod POD

troubleshoots.symptom: 'no scraped data for X yet' when running query/next-cls
troubleshoots.fix: Run schedule-pp-cli pull --route X first to populate the local store.

troubleshoots.symptom: Carrier-services or vessels list looks short
troubleshoots.fix: Some lanes have '10日内无计划开航' status — Weiyun has no published sailings in the 10-day window. Check schedule-pp-cli compare-carriers to confirm.

narrative.when_to_use: Use this CLI when an agent needs ocean-freight schedule data for a forwarder/NVOCC/BCO. The API layer (ports, carriers, fleet-routes, carrier-services) supports lane discovery; the registry layer (pull, query, next-cls, compare-carriers) supports daily 08:30 schedule briefings.
